questions.quote: Note: As the positive charge increases the size of the cation decreases. As the negative charge increases the size of the anion increases.

en.q: Which of the following statements is correct for ions?
options: The size of an ion does not depend on its charge
As the negative charge increases the anion becomes smaller
As the positive charge increases the cation becomes larger
Cations shrink and anions grow with increasing charge
en.explanation: Fluorine and chlorine become anions by gaining electrons; the nuclear charge cannot hold the larger number of electrons as tightly.

questions.quote: More to Know: Noble gases show no tendency to accept electrons because the outer s and p orbitals of noble gases are completely filled. No more electrons can be added to them and hence their electron affinities are zero.

en.q: Noble gases have zero electron affinity because
options: they have very large atomic size
their outer s and p orbitals are completely filled
they have high ionisation energy only
en.explanation: No more electrons can be added to them.

questions.quote: More to Know: Extraction of metal from metal oxide can be categorized into three types. More reactive metals Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al - electrolytic reduction; medium reactive Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu - chemical reduction using coke; less reactive Ag, Hg - thermal decomposition.

en.q: Which pair correctly matches the metal with the method of reduction of its oxide?
options: Aluminium – electrolytic reduction; zinc – reduction with coke; mercury – thermal decomposition
Sodium – coke; iron – electrolysis; silver – electrolysis
Aluminium – thermal decomposition; zinc – electrolysis; mercury – coke
Mercury – electrolysis; copper – thermal decomposition; calcium – coke
en.explanation: The method depends on the reactivity of the metal.

Consider the following statements:

(iii) A periodic table arranges elements in rows and columns in regular gradation.

en.explanation: All three statements are taken from the lesson.
